review_notes: Principal scope: the paper’s registered average-treatment question is whether a small Starbucks stock investment changes product purchases and regulatory alignment (H1/H2, physical PDF p. 9). The selected planned baseline results are Table 2, panels A–C (physical PDF p. 18), as explicitly described as planned hypothesis tests comparing OwnMoney, OthersMoney, and RegulatoryAlignment across experimental conditions. The paper reports independent-samples t-tests for OwnMoney and RegulatoryAlignment and a chi-squared test for OthersMoney; these are group comparisons, not regressions, so no baseline regression is eligible for schema 1.

Excluded: Table 4’s regressions are explicitly planned supplemental moderator analyses (physical PDF pp. 21–25); Table 5 panel A tests social-connection interactions (physical PDF pp. 25–27); the multivariate tests with controls are identified as robustness tests and are untabulated (physical PDF p. 31). They are later supplementary/robustness work and do not replace the authors’ selected Table 2 baseline tests.
descriptive_reason: No baseline regression was retained, so there are no retained regression variables for model-linked descriptive statistics.
results_review_notes: Table 1 reports descriptive statistics for the paper’s variables, but the principal registered tests are non-regression group comparisons and no regression models or variables are retained in this extraction.

calculation_provenance.policy: strict; no guessed degrees of freedom or normal approximations
